podcast.body: This song is explicitly compared to Richie Valens' "Ooh My Head," with the suggestion that Valens' composition evolved from performing and modifying Little Richard's original. Little Richard notably did not pursue legal action for this appropriation. "You can see that Valence's song seems to have come from precisely this process, of performing someone else's song, and changing it around until it became something different."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs

podcast.body: This song, described as one of Little Richard's "very best records," was recorded during the same productive session in early 1957 that produced "Keep a-Knockin'." "At the same session, he also recorded another of his very best records. Oh my soul."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs
